articles.title: Who Can Take Justin Gaethje’s Belt? #ufc
articles.description: If Justin Gaethje's next fight really is his last, the UFC has a problem. Chael Sonnen believes that if Gaethje is considering retirement, there's a very real possibility that his next fight could be his final appearance in the Octagon. And if that's the case, the stakes become even higher. The UFC doesn't want its champion walking away with the belt. That's where the potential matchups with Paddy Pimblett and Ilia Topuria come into play. If Chael had to choose between the two as Gaethje's next opponent, he'd lean toward Paddy — largely because of the damage and recovery involved. But the bigger question is which fighter is actually equipped to take the belt away from Gaethje. Gaethje is one of the most dangerous punchers in the sport. His pressure, durability, and power make every matchup a problem, especially when there's a championship on the line. And if the UFC knows this could be his last fight, Chael believes the people making the matchup have one job: Get the belt back. They can't publicly say that's the objective, but that's exactly what the situation demands. So between Paddy Pimblett and Ilia Topuria, who is best equipped to beat Justin Gaethje and prevent him from walking away as champion? #JustinGaethje #PaddyPimblett #IliaTopuria #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #BMF #CombatSports

articles.title: Conor McGregor’s Infamous Grand Arrival Confrontation | This Day in MMA: Aug. 22
articles.description: This Day in MMA: Conor McGregor’s Infamous Grand Arrival Confrontation | Aug. 22 August 22, 2017. Four days before Floyd Mayweather and Conor McGregor, the Grand Arrival at T-Mobile Arena fell apart on the red carpet. McGregor had already promised a short night — he was struggling to give Mayweather two rounds. Then he and Floyd had to be pulled apart by their own security. And then Paulie Malignaggi walked up on him. Malignaggi had sparred McGregor in that camp and walked out of it, and the photos went out anyway. He wanted an answer: "Did you bring your balls, Conor?" He had a prediction, too — McGregor was going to fold again on Saturday. Across the same carpet, Floyd Mayweather was calmer, and more specific: this fight wouldn't go the distance. If you're gonna bet, bet it won't go. Four days later he stopped him in the tenth. articles.title: 22 Years Ago Today: Randy Couture Took the Title Back at 41 🏆
articles.description: 22 Years Ago Today: Randy Couture Took the Title Back at 41 August 21, 2004. MGM Grand. Randy Couture and Vitor Belfort had already fought twice, and neither fight had settled anything. The first time, back at UFC 15 in 1997, Couture stopped him with punches in round one. The second, in January 2004, Belfort's glove caught Couture's eyelid forty-nine seconds in — the doctor waved it off and Belfort walked out with the light heavyweight title. They called the rubber match Unfinished Business. This time there was no accident. Couture controlled all three rounds, and at the end of the third the doctor looked at Belfort's eye and ended it. Forty-one years old, and Randy Couture was champion again. Two wins to one. Three fights, three finishes. Nobody ever needed a fourth. Twenty-two years ago today. articles.title: Who Is Really Next for Islam Makhachev? #ufc
articles.description: Carlos Prates says he's next for Islam Makhachev. But Chael Sonnen isn't convinced that's how this should play out. There's now a potential problem at the top of the division: Carlos Prates and Michael Morales both have legitimate arguments to be next in line. One suggestion has been to simply put them against each other and let the winner become the undisputed No. 1 contender. Sounds logical. But Chael sees a major downside. If two legitimate contenders fight each other, you eliminate one potential title fight. And if the UFC doesn't need them to fight each other to determine who's next, why remove one of those options? There's also the question of what happens to Islam while that fight takes place. If Morales and Prates have to fight first, Islam could potentially be sitting on the shelf while the UFC determines his next challenger. Chael's preference is clear: he doesn't want to eliminate either contender. Morales has an especially strong case. Chael points out that it was reportedly Dana White who told Morales he was next following his huge victory at Madison Square Garden. Prates is certainly dangerous and has plenty of support inside the UFC. But Chael believes Morales is the guy who should be fighting Islam. So who actually gets the next title shot? And should Morales and Prates really be forced to eliminate each other first? #IslamMakhachev #MichaelMorales #CarlosPrates #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #UFCTitle #CombatSports

articles.title: Beating Ian Garry Doesn’t Make Islam the GOAT #ufc
articles.description: Is Islam Makhachev really the greatest fighter of all time? Chael Sonnen isn't ready to give him that title. The biggest problem with the argument is simple: Jon Jones still exists. Chael argues that Jones has never had his weaknesses truly identified and exploited by an opponent. Until somebody figures out exactly how to beat Jones and actually does it, it's difficult to simply move him out of the GOAT conversation. And Chael has another problem with the way Islam's status is being discussed. Beating Ian Garry was impressive. But is beating a young fighter with tremendous length and range — who was also trying to maintain respect and sportsmanship throughout the fight — really enough to establish yourself as the greatest mixed martial artist of all time? Chael says no. The GOAT conversation shouldn't change every time a champion wins a major fight. If it did, the title would simply belong to whoever won the most recent main event — at least until the next big performance comes along. Islam is unquestionably one of the greatest fighters in the sport. But greatest of all time requires something more. Head-to-head competition. More elite wins. More championship accomplishments. More opportunities to prove yourself across different challenges and, potentially, different weight classes. Islam may eventually have that résumé. Chael just doesn't believe he's there yet. So where do you stand? Is Islam already the GOAT, or does Jon Jones still own that spot? #IslamMakhachev #JonJones #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #GOAT #MMAHistory #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #CombatSports

articles.title: Alex Pereira vs. Josh Hokit Makes Perfect Sense
articles.description: Alex Pereira and Josh Hokit already had unfinished business. Now there may be a very good reason to settle it inside the Octagon. Chael Sonnen reacts to Glover Teixeira suggesting Pereira and Hokit fight with a UFC heavyweight title opportunity on the line. After their heated press conference interaction, both men now have open dance cards, and Pereira appears ready to revisit the matchup. But the heavyweight championship situation complicates everything. Tom Aspinall remains the undisputed champion, Ciryl Gane holds the interim title, and Chael says even people behind the scenes aren't certain whether the UFC will be able to make Aspinall vs. Gane next. If that fight doesn't happen, Hokit could potentially find himself opposite Gane instead. If Aspinall and Gane do unify the titles, however, Chael sees another solution: put Pereira vs. Hokit on the same card as the backup fight and treat it as a No. 1 contender matchup. articles.title: This Day in MMA August 20: McGregor vs Diaz UFC 202
articles.description: Ten years ago tonight, Conor McGregor and Nate Diaz went to war at UFC 202. Nate Diaz had submitted McGregor just six months earlier at UFC 196, handing the Irish superstar his first UFC loss. McGregor demanded the rematch at 170 pounds. What followed became one of the most memorable fights in UFC history. McGregor dropped Diaz three times early, but Diaz refused to go away. He rallied as the fight progressed, turning the third round into a war and pushing McGregor through all five rounds. McGregor ultimately won by majority decision, evening their rivalry at 1-1. After the fight, McGregor couldn’t help but respect Diaz’s toughness: 🗣️ “One man’s face was opened up and he’s still just coming. He’s still just coming. You’ve got to respect that. You’ve got to respect Nate and the style of fighting that he brings. How can you not?” Diaz, however, never believed he’d lost. 🗣️ “I didn’t think for a second that I lost.” August 20, 2016 → August 20, 2026. Ten years later, Conor McGregor and Nate Diaz remain tied 1-1 — and MMA fans are still waiting for the trilogy. articles.title: Beating Ian Garry Does NOT Make Islam the GOAT
articles.description: Is Islam Makhachev really the greatest mixed martial artist of all time, or are we once again handing out GOAT status immediately after a big UFC main event? Chael Sonnen questions why the GOAT conversation around Islam exploded after his victory over Ian Machado Garry. If beating Garry is the accomplishment that pushed Islam over the top, what does that say about Shavkat Rakhmonov, who also defeated Garry while maintaining an undefeated record? Then there's Jon Jones. Chael argues that any greatest-of-all-time discussion becomes extremely difficult when Jones' career exists, particularly when we've never definitively established the weaknesses an opponent could exploit. Chael also compares Islam's approach as champion with Alexander Volkanovski's willingness to fight whoever has earned the opportunity, whenever and wherever the fight is offered. Islam deserves enormous respect for everything he's accomplished, but Chael isn't ready to crown him based on one more win. articles.title: Has Islam Earned the Right to Be Above Ilia?#ufc
articles.description: How can Islam Makhachev be ranked ahead of Ilia Topuria? That's the question Chael Sonnen is asking. After Ilia's latest loss, the two fighters now have something important in common: one career loss and one stoppage loss. But Chael argues that the circumstances surrounding those losses matter. Ilia's loss came in a massive main event on the White House lawn against elite competition. Islam's only loss came much earlier in his career. So does recency really change the argument? Chael also brings up something Islam doesn't particularly enjoy discussing: Islam turned down a fight with Ilia. To be fair, Islam had a reason. He argued that Ilia hadn't fought at lightweight yet and wanted him to establish himself at 155 pounds before fighting the champion. But Chael points out that Islam himself had previously made similar moves when other fighters challenged him. Now there's another issue. When asked about potential opponents like Michael Morales and Benoît Saint Denis, Islam's answer was essentially: have them fight each other. Chael's question is whether that eventually becomes another form of avoiding a direct challenge. Because if you're going to call someone the greatest fighter in the world, what happens when that fighter starts saying no to fights? Is Islam still clearly ahead of Ilia? Or is the gap between them much smaller than people think? #IslamMakhachev #IliaTopuria #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #IslamVsIlia #UFCGOAT #CombatSports

articles.title: Ian Garry Was Too Focused on Islam’s Approval #ufc
articles.description: Ian Garry didn't lose because he lacked skill. Chael Sonnen believes the bigger issue was mindset. Throughout the fight, Chael saw Garry repeatedly seeking Islam Makhachev's approval instead of treating him like the man standing between him and a UFC championship. Garry praised Islam as the greatest fighter in the world. He continued reaching out to him between rounds and after the fight. Meanwhile, Islam was telling him to stop talking. For Chael, that's the problem. When you're fighting someone at this level, respect is one thing. But you're not there to make your opponent like you. You're there to take the championship from him. Chael believes Garry didn't behave like a young fighter who had come into the Octagon prepared to take the title by force. And that's especially important when you're losing rounds. Once a round is gone, you can't get it back. There is no reason to spend that time worrying about how the other team perceives you. The comparison to the famous Khabib-Conor McGregor rivalry makes the point even stronger. Chael wonders whether Garry was expecting some kind of mutual respect or acknowledgment after the fight instead of approaching it like a championship fight where only one man gets what he came for. Garry showed plenty of skill and toughness. But Chael believes he needs to overcome one thing moving forward: Stop worrying about being liked. Start believing you belong at the top. #IanGarry #IslamMakhachev #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #UFCChampionship #IanGarryUFC #CombatSports

articles.title: Why Did Islam Makhachev Wear Two Belts?
articles.description: Why is Islam Makhachev walking around with two UFC championship belts? Chael Sonnen looks at the photos of Islam following his welterweight title win and explains an important distinction: being a champion in two divisions is not the same thing as being a simultaneous “champ champ.” Islam was previously the UFC lightweight champion, but he gave up that title before becoming welterweight champion. So why does he have two belts? Chael goes back to Conor McGregor becoming a true simultaneous two-division champion against Eddie Alvarez, including the wild story of the UFC borrowing Tyron Woodley’s belt when they realized Conor needed a second one in the Octagon. He also uses Ilia Topuria and the BMF title to explain why actually winning a belt under the terms of a championship fight matters. The larger issue is how UFC history gets recorded. Winning a championship, defending a championship and reclaiming a championship are different accomplishments. If we're going to talk about champions and their legacies, Chael argues we should get the history right. So the question remains: who gave Islam that second belt? #UFC #IslamMakhachev #ChaelSonnen #ConorMcGregor #IliaTopuria #JonJones #MMA Bad Guy Inc merch now available at https://BadGuyInc.com Click here to subscribe: https://bit.ly/3FrHIPK Follow me on IG: https://bit.ly/3HY7BIE Follow me on Twitter: https://bit.ly/3tvY5J7 Follow me on Threads https://www.threads.com/@sonnench

articles.title: Ian Garry Was Too Nice to Islam #ufc
articles.description: Ian Garry fought well against Islam Makhachev. But Chael Sonnen believes there was one mental mistake Garry may eventually regret. According to Chael, Garry spent too much time trying to be liked by Islam instead of treating him like the obstacle standing between him and a UFC championship. The pep talks during the fight. The praise between rounds. The post-fight respect. Even telling people that Islam is the greatest fighter in the world. Chael's question is simple: Why are you trying to make this guy feel good? This was Garry's first UFC title fight, and Chael understands that he's still a young fighter learning how to handle the biggest moments of his career. But he believes there may come a point, weeks after the fight, when Garry looks back and wishes he had trusted himself more. Because the assignment was clear: get up. And Garry understood it. He repeatedly scrambled, fought to return to his feet, and showed the wrestling IQ and determination needed to compete with Islam's control game. That matters. Chael isn't criticizing Garry's performance. He's questioning the mindset surrounding it. You don't have to hate your opponent. But when you're fighting for the world championship, you have to believe you're better than the man standing across from you. Did Ian Garry show too much respect for Islam? #IanGarry #IslamMakhachev #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #UFCFight #IanGarryUFC #CombatSports

articles.title: Dana Calls Out Joshua & Fury: 'You Wanna Fight or Not?'

articles.title: Islam Looked Unbeatable… #ufc
articles.description: Is Islam Makhachev actually unbeatable? Chael Sonnen isn't ready to say yes. Ian Garry didn't expose a clear weakness in Islam's game, but he may have shown that a weakness could exist. Despite facing moments that could have frustrated a normal fighter, Islam stayed composed, handled the pressure, and performed at an extremely high level. Daniel Cormier also pointed out just how much was riding on this fight. Islam wasn't simply defending his reputation — he was fighting under the pressure of potentially breaking Anderson Silva's historic UFC win-streak record. And somehow, Islam still looked incredibly complete. But now Chael is looking at a new name: Michael Morales. Before this fight, the idea of Morales fighting Islam wasn't particularly compelling to Chael. Now it is. Why? Morales may be able to defend takedowns more effectively than Garry. He's explosive, dangerous, and brings serious power. Chael isn't claiming Morales is a better striker than Ian Garry — but he believes Morales may hit harder. If Morales can force Islam to work in areas where Garry couldn't, could he become the first fighter to genuinely expose a hole in Islam's game? Islam may still be the favorite. But for the first time, Chael sees a matchup that makes him genuinely curious. Islam Makhachev vs. Michael Morales just got interesting. #IslamMakhachev #MichaelMorales #IanGarry #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #IslamMakhachevUFC #CombatSports

articles.title: Is Islam REALLY the Best Fighter in the World?
articles.description: After an exchange with MMA Junkie's Danny Segura, Chael takes issue with the idea that bigger welterweights are preventing Islam from finishing opponents. Islam and Ian Machado Garry both weighed 170 pounds before their fight, and Islam has already proven he belongs in the division by becoming its champion. But the argument leads to a bigger question. If Islam is the best fighter on the planet, why is he telling Michael Morales and Carlos Prates to fight each other rather than accepting either challenge? articles.title: Din Thomas Gave the Perfect Apology
articles.description: Dean Thomas apologized for announcing his retirement from cornering immediately after Jillian Robertson's fight with Mackenzie Dern. Chael Sonnen believes the apology deserves to be accepted. Chael explains why Dean's response was more than simply saying “I'm sorry.” Dean took responsibility, acknowledged that the timing took attention away from Jillian, and backed his words with action. In Chael's view, it was about as sincere an apology as someone can give. But Chael also thinks Dean may be too hard on himself. Jillian Robertson never stopped fighting, proved she could perform through championship rounds, and even took the fifth round from Mackenzie Dern.
